# Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospitaler

Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospitaler is a major hospital entity operating within the [[region-hovedstaden|Capital Region of Denmark]] (Region Hovedstaden). As part of the [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Capital Region total]], it is systematically evaluated in the national Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) reports, which monitor clinical quality, patient outcomes, and process indicators for acute high-risk abdominal surgery.

During the reporting period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023, the hospital demonstrated notable performance across several quality metrics. Most significantly, it achieved a 38.0% compliance rate for [[indikator-1|Indicator 1]] (antibiotic treatment within three hours), marking the highest proportion among the individual hospitals listed in the national table [^src1]. The hospital also recorded the highest unit compliance for [[indikator-8|Indicator 8]] (early nutritional assessment) at 53.9% [^src3]. However, its compliance for the supplementary [[indikator-5x|Indicator 5x]] (speed of surgical intervention for life-threatening conditions) was measured at 22.6% [^src2]. 

In terms of patient demographics and outcomes for the 2022–2023 period, the hospital treated 231 operated patients with specific cancer distributions, including 14 cases of gastrointestinal cancers and 4 cases of other cancers [^src4]. Postoperative mortality tracking revealed that 5 out of 83 patients with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score of 1 or 2]] died within 30 days following acute surgery, representing a 6.0% mortality rate [^src5]. The hospital's age and demographic distributions are also systematically recorded for regional benchmarking [^src6].

Subsequent data from the 2024 AKDB report (covering September 2023 to August 2024) shows continued monitoring of these metrics. The hospital's compliance for Indicator 1 was recorded at 29.3% [^src7], and its performance on Indicator 5x was 15.1% [^src8]. Mortality among patients with a Charlson Score of 1 or 2 saw 7 out of 73 patients dying within 30 days (9.6%) [^src9], while demographic and age distribution tracking remained a core component of the hospital's quality reporting [^src10].
